wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: no roles, peers or directions exist in a pure HTML sanitizer; every destination is evaluated by the same policy
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the sanitizer has no read/write split; it only transforms a value into output
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: entity decoding and transformTags both run before every scheme check, so no adjusting step sits between the attacker value and the guarded sink that a patch could move the check behind
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: there is no authority, secret or role lookup that could fail open in this library

notes: The published fix (1135516a) changes only packages/sanitize-html/index.js plus README/docs/tests. All hidden tests drive the public sanitizeHtml(html, options) entry point in-process. The environment installs the package's dependency tree into /opt/app-deps (NODE_PATH) so the verifier needs no network and no node_modules inside the restored artifact. The frozen project suite is a copy of packages/sanitize-html/test/test.js at the pinned commit (which does not contain the advisory's regression tests). Browser execution semantics of javascript: in a refresh destination were not verified; the tests assert the forbidden destination is not emitted, which is what the upstream fix enforces.
